info.title: Library Management System API
info.description:
REST API for a library management system — books, authors, users, and the borrow/return workflow, with role-based access control (Admin/Librarian/User).

This document is generated from JSDoc annotations on the route files (`npm run docs:generate`) — do not hand-edit `docs/API.md` or `src/openapi.json`.

bearerAuth.description: Obtain a token from `POST /auth/register`, `POST /auth/login`, or `POST /auth/setup-admin`, then send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but wrong role or not the resource owner

example.message: Access denied. Required role(s): Admin. Your role: User
Too many requests from this IP, please try again after 15 minutes

get.summary: Get the current user's full profile, with borrowing statistics

post.description: Requires the Admin role. Can create any role, unlike self-registration.

get.description: Requires the Admin/Librarian role, or that the caller is requesting their own profile.

put.description: Requires the resource owner, a Librarian, or an Admin. Which fields a given caller may actually set is enforced server-side and depends on who's calling — see the field-restriction table in `docs/API.md`. Attempting to set `role` without the Admin role returns 403; every other disallowed field is silently dropped rather than rejected.

403.description: Not the resource owner/Librarian/Admin, or attempted to set `role` without Admin.

409.description: Email already taken by another user.

delete.description: Requires the Admin role. Fails if the user has active borrows, or is the last active Admin.

409.description: User has active borrows, or is the last active Admin.

new_password.description: 8+ characters, at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one number. Must differ from the current password.

post.description: Always responds 200 with the same generic message, whether or not the email is registered, to avoid leaking which emails exist. If the account exists, emails a single-use, 1-hour reset token (or logs it server-side as a dev-mode fallback if SMTP isn't configured) — the token itself is never returned in this response.

example.message: If an account with that email exists, a password reset link has been sent.

post.description: Authorization comes from possessing a valid reset token, not from a session. Single-use — a second attempt with the same token returns 400.

400.description: Invalid, expired, or already-used reset token; or validation failure.
